label: CONSERVED_FUNCTIONAL_BENCHMARK_v1
what: Six ACCUMULATION boards whose conserved replacement is already known. A proposer sees the before-board and its leak, never the after-board, and is scored on whether it names the functional that worked -- or one an adversary cannot kill.
why_six: These are every ACCUMULATION item in the corpus (5) plus the trio's K1 -> K3, which is the exemplar the taxonomy was induced from. Six is small. It is six more than a pipeline with no benchmark has.
blinding: The proposer is given: state, move, invariant, composition and the leak sentence. It is NOT given the after-board, the paper, the year, or the names. The recognition probe from the protocol tree applies -- ask it to name the problem, and record the answer, because D25 measured that a rater who recognises the problem needs no rule.

scoring.hit: names the functional that worked, or an equivalent one, before seeing the after-board
scoring.survivor: names a functional the adversary cannot kill, which is not the historical one -- recorded separately, because a second conserved functional is a real result
scoring.relocation: names a functional that moves the loss elsewhere; the agent is asked to say so itself (Check 3), and gets credit for saying it
scoring.not_applicable: declines. The NA rate is a first-class number, as prospective.py says of the diagnostic.

items.degrading: Gaussian measure of a symmetric convex body stays >= 1/2, and degrades under each application of the move
items.move: replace the body by a convex subset of the union of its two translates
items.conserved_answer: directional total variation of a density supported on the body, preserved exactly under the move

items.degrading: density increment delta -> delta + c delta^2 over about 1/delta iterations, each costing one dimension
items.move: large Fourier coefficient, then restrict to a hyperplane
items.conserved_answer: slice rank -- a one-shot bound with no iteration at all

items.degrading: matrix Chernoff on E||Sigma_S||; the factor n in tr exp gives log n, tight on direct sums of independent blocks
items.conserved_answer: the largest root of the expected characteristic polynomial: for a direct sum it is the MAXIMUM over blocks, so the bound is dimension-free

items.degrading: per-set Chernoff bound composed by a union bound over n sets, which is where the sqrt(log n) comes from
items.conserved_answer: entropy of a partial colouring -- a global count that does not pay per set

items.degrading: a recursive inequality on J where each iteration recovers a fixed fraction of the defect, so about log k rounds are needed
items.conserved_answer: efficient congruencing: maintain congruence conditions at every scale simultaneously, removing the accumulation over rounds

items.degrading: value decay under k-fold repetition, with instance size multiplicative in the exponent (n^k)
items.conserved_answer: graph powering on expanders plus alphabet reduction, with constant-factor size blow-up

not_runnable_here: No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and no model access in this container -- the same wall as debt D18. The harness to run it exists at proof-protocol/p2-ablation/, fidelity-tested against the published artifact's own JavaScript.
first_thing_to_check_when_it_runs: the recognition probe. If a proposer names the problem, D25 applies and a hit tells you nothing about the screen -- it tells you the model remembers Ellenberg-Gijswijt. The only uncontaminated items would be boards whose transformation does not exist yet, which is why FINDER.md section 4 points at 2609.11189's own three open leaks.
